RFC9012-13-14.note: Independent first judgment against the complete RFC 9012 Section 13 sentence: "There is one exception to this rule: if a TLV contains a malformed Tunnel Egress Endpoint sub-TLV (as defined in Section 3.1), the entire TLV MUST be ignored and MUST be removed from the Tunnel Encapsulation attribute before the route carrying that attribute is distributed." TestRFC9012EndpointInvalidTLVsRemovedOnUnicast meaningfully proves structural removal on IPv4 unicast: missing or duplicate endpoints, a too-short endpoint, short IPv4 and IPv6 values, and an overlong AFI-zero value either remove only the offending TLVs around a valid sibling or yield exact TreatAsWithdraw when none survive. It compares the complete repaired UPDATE, unchanged source input and source identity. For a surviving sibling, teForwardedAttrs exercises real processMessage receive dispatch, ForwardUpdate, default and MED-policy-rebuilt export, socket output and downstream processMessage, with exact retained bytes and NLRI assertions. applyTunnelEncap publishes the rebuilt body and attributes, so the removed TLVs are not handed to that consumer. Nevertheless, the sentence imports every Section 3.1 malformed-endpoint condition: tunnelEndpointLengthValid checks encoded length and AFI only, not the Special-Purpose IP Address registry conditions or determinable origin-AS mismatch; the tests likewise assert no such address-semantic case. The no-survivor branch asserts a classification rather than downstream withdrawal. Existing producer-panic discrimination records establish dependence on applyTunnelEncap, not these absent clauses. Retain weak: structural removal is real and tested, but whole-requirement enforcement is not established. No optional origin-AS-validation feature or new proof scope is authorized.

RFC9012-13-15.note: Independent first judgment against RFC 9012 Section 13: "Within a Tunnel Encapsulation attribute that is carried by a BGP UPDATE whose AFI/SAFI is one of those explicitly listed in the first paragraph of Section 6, a TLV that does not contain exactly one Tunnel Egress Endpoint sub-TLV MUST be treated as if it contained a malformed Tunnel Egress Endpoint sub-TLV." TestRFC9012EndpointInvalidTLVsRemovedOnUnicast supplies a valid one-endpoint control and genuine missing/duplicate-endpoint violations using teCarryBody's legacy IPv4-unicast NLRI. It checks removal around a valid sibling through default and rebuilt socket forwarding, and exact TreatAsWithdraw when none survive. The producer counts endpoints and applies the requirement to legacy IPv4 NLRI and MP_REACH AFI 1/2 SAFI 1/4/128 plus AFI 25 SAFI 70, excluding the separately specified SR Policy behavior. However, this tagged unit never constructs those other Section 6 MP_REACH carriers; a broken carrier-selection branch for IPv6 unicast, labeled unicast, VPN or EVPN would leave its assertions unchanged. The no-survivor branch also does not assert downstream withdrawal dispatch. Current producer-panic records do not supply that missing carrier or downstream oracle. Keep weak for the full carrier-scoped obligation while crediting the actual IPv4-unicast structural count/removal evidence; do not expand tags, features or declared proof scope.
